01 / Brand Essence

One cube. Three dimensions. A world of art.

KalaCUBE should feel like a living cultural universe rather than a static art directory. The platform connects creators, audiences, stories, objects, performances, workshops and communities.

“KalaCUBE is the place where creativity can be seen, touched and experienced.”

Purpose

Make art easier to discover, understand, experience and support — across disciplines and cultures.

Vision

Build a global digital home for artists, makers and performers where every form of creativity has a place.

Promise

Every visit should reveal something creative, human and worth remembering.

02 / Logo System

The cube is the brand.

The cube is not decoration. It is the core metaphor: multiple faces, multiple disciplines, one ecosystem. Keep it recognizable at every size.

Logo architecture

Kala = art / creativity / culture. CUBE = a multi-dimensional space. The three visible faces represent the three core creative dimensions.

  • Primary lockup: cube symbol + कलाCUBE wordmark.
  • Compact mark: cube / CK symbol for favicon, app icon and small UI.
  • Monochrome version: for embossing, documents and one-colour production.
  • Dark-background version: white wordmark with the colour cube.

Clear space: keep at least the height of the yellow square around the logo on all sides. Never squeeze, rotate, stretch, recolour randomly or place it on visually noisy imagery.

03 / The Three Dimensions

Three creative worlds inside one cube.

These are first-class categories in navigation, search, profiles, editorial content and landing-page storytelling.

✦

VISUAL ART

Painting, illustration, photography, digital art, sculpture, mixed media, installations and emerging visual practices.

Brand feeling: See · Imagine · Create
◆

HANDICRAFT

Pottery, textiles, jewellery, woodworking, weaving, ceramics, traditional craft and contemporary making.

Brand feeling: Feel · Make · Preserve
✦

PERFORMING ART

Dance, music, theatre, spoken word, cultural performance and live creative experiences.

Brand feeling: Experience · Express · Connect

05 / Typography

Modern enough for digital. Warm enough for culture.

Poppins

Primary UI family. Use for navigation, buttons, labels, cards, headings and short marketing copy.

Weights: 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800.

Editorial display

Use a refined serif or high-contrast display face sparingly for campaign headlines and storytelling. It should feel like a contemporary cultural magazine, not a corporate SaaS dashboard.

06 / Visual Direction

Gallery meets digital universe.

Photography

Prefer real artists, real hands, real materials, real performances and real spaces. Show process, texture and emotion rather than generic stock imagery.

Composition

Use generous negative space, strong crops, layered imagery and occasional full-bleed visual moments. Let artwork be the hero.

Motion

Subtle cube rotations, image reveals, flowing ribbons and category transitions are welcome. Avoid excessive parallax or distracting animation.

Image rule

Never make AI-generated decoration more important than the artist. The platform exists to elevate creators and their work.

07 / Website Experience

Redesign KalaCUBE.com as a discovery platform, not a brochure.

The current site is a JavaScript application, so the redesign should preserve the underlying product direction while replacing the experience with a more intentional visual system. (reviewed September 2026)

Homepage flow

  1. Hero: “A World of Art. In One Cube.”
  2. Three dimensions

Experience principleImplementation
Discover firstSearch and browse should be immediately visible; users should reach an artist or artwork in 1–2 interactions.
Three dimensionsPersistent category language and colour coding across cards, filters, profiles and breadcrumbs.
Artist-firstArtist identity, story, medium, location/culture, work and links are more important than platform decoration.
CommunityEvents, workshops and collaborations should feel like living activity, not an afterthought.
Mobile-firstCards become swipeable; cube mark remains clear; category colour remains accessible without relying on colour alone.
08 / UI Visual Guide

Component language

Buttons

Primary: Navy background, white text.
Action: Yellow background, navy text.
Secondary: White/cream with navy border.

Cards

18–24px radius, soft shadow, large imagery, concise metadata and clear creator attribution. Avoid dense dashboard styling.

Tags

Use compact pills for medium, location, discipline, event type and availability. Category tags use the three dimension colours.

Spacing

Use an 8px base grid. Desktop section spacing 72–96px; mobile 48–64px. Give artwork room to breathe.

Shape language

Rounded rectangles + occasional cube geometry. The cube is the distinctive form; don't turn every component into a cube.

Accessibility

Maintain strong contrast, visible focus states, keyboard navigation, alt text for artwork, captions for video and never communicate meaning through colour alone.

09 / Brand Voice

Human. Curious. Celebratory. Inclusive.

Say

  • Discover an artist you haven't met yet.
  • Made by hand. Rooted in story.
  • Experience art beyond the frame.
  • One platform. A thousand stories.
  • Bring art closer to the world.

Avoid

  • Overly corporate “solutions / users / assets” language.
  • Making creators sound like inventory.
  • Generic “revolutionary platform” claims.
  • Excessive jargon.
  • Using “Kala” as a decorative word without cultural meaning.
Core message
CREATE. CRAFT. PERFORM. DISCOVER. CONNECT.
